title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' draft, Grothendieck works with 'figures'. A figure F consists of a support |F| = X (a closed, tame or semi-algebraic-type subset) together with a locally finite partition of X into strata X_i. The partition is compatible with closures, so it amounts to an equivalence relation on X. A figure is 'elementary' when it is the closure of a single open stratum with its induced stratification. The previous page identified closed subfigures with configurations of elementary figures. This page defines subdivision, reducing first to the 'cas-type' of a single figure.

Definition: F' is a subdivision of F if (a) |F'| = |F| and (b) the equivalence relation on X = |F| defined by F' (being in the same stratum) is finer than the one defined by F.

Reformulation (b'): for every stratum X_i of F, X_i is a union of strata of F'. Grothendieck notes that (b') is equivalent to (b).

Consequence: the strata of F' contained in the closure of X_i form a figure with support that closure. This figure is a subdivision of F_{X̄_i}, the elementary figure induced by F on the closure of X_i.

Caveat: this induced subdivision need not be elementary. A subdivision of an elementary figure can have several top-dimensional open strata. Example: a segment cut at an interior point into two edges.

On the next page this leads to a second order relation on elementary figures, 'raffine' (F' ≪ F: every open stratum of F' lies in an open stratum of F). This order is finer than inclusion and lets subdivision be read off elementary pieces. The purpose of the page is to set up the combinatorics of refinement of stratifications needed for a tame-topology foundation in the spirit of 'topologie modérée' in the Esquisse.
errors: No substantive error. Implicitly the strata of F' inside X̄_i must form a closed sub-configuration. This holds because strata of F' contained in X̄_i have closures in X̄_i (X̄_i is closed and a union of F'-strata by (b')). The page does not spell this out.
Equivalence of (b) and (b') is immediate since both are partitions of the same set; the word 'implique' followed by 'est équivalente' is just a self-correction.

ideas.what: Subdivision of a stratified 'figure': same support, finer partition into strata.
ideas.modern_name: refinement of a stratification / subdivision (PL or cell-complex refinement, refinement of a semialgebraic or o-minimal stratification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical: PL topology (Whitehead, Hauptvermutung era); Thom-Mather and o-minimal literature (van den Dries) for stratifications
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame topology and stratified structures in general terms, without this formal definition

ideas.what: Restriction of a subdivision to the closure of each stratum gives a subdivision of the induced elementary figure, which need not itself be elementary.
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a refinement to closed strata / cells; a subdivided cell is not a cell
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard folklore in PL / CW / regular cell complex theory

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational definition of refinement and subdivision for stratified figures in Grothendieck's tame-topology draft. It is historically interesting as part of the unpublished 'Analysis situs', but the mathematics is standard.
transcription_corrections: 'formée de X et de [-?-] de ses strates X_i' likely reads 'formée de X et de la partition de X en ses strates X_i' (a crossed-out word precedes it).
'Une figure F' qui est une subdivision de F est une [?] définie' probably reads 'est une [figure] définie par les propriétés' or 'est caractérisée par'.
'& elle est = équivalente' likely reads 'et elle lui est équivalente', i.e. (b') is equivalent to (b).

'les strates pour F' qui sont ⊂ [-X_i-] X_i': the replacement is most likely X̄_i (closure). The same applies to 'F_{X_i}' → F_{X̄_i} and 'de support X_i' → X̄_i, since an elementary figure is supported on a closed stratum.
'n'est pas nécessairement élémentaire' is correctly read; the final parenthesis reads '(une subdivision d'une figure élém. peut n'être pas élémentaire)'.
